description:
We are NASAPOLLITES, a passionate team of builders, coders, and space enthusiasts taking on the SPHEREx challenge at NASA Space Apps 2026. NASA’s SPHEREx mission maps the entire sky across 102 near-infrared bands, holding the secrets to undiscovered brown dwarfs, comets, asteroids, and variable stars, but the sheer volume of data is far too vast for any single team of astronomers to sift through alone.

Our mission is to bridge that gap by building an intuitive, public-facing web tool! :)
summary: Astro Sentinella is more than a web app, it is an interactive time-domain astrophysics and spectral visualization platform for NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Prioritizing accuracy, fast loading times, and an intuitive design, it allows anyone to explore, gather information, and make insights from every single bit of data that this mission has to offer.
details:
Designed as a browser-based discovery environment, Astro Sentinella streamlines the exploration and comparison of multi-epoch near-infrared observations from NASA’s SPHEREx archive. Users enter celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) or choose preconfigured targets alongside specific observation dates, detector bands, and fields of view.

When a comparison is requested, the backend retrieves calibrated FITS images and World Coordinate System (WCS) metadata from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), crops the target sky region, and reprojects one epoch onto the other’s exact pixel grid. It then models and subtracts smooth two-dimensional sky backgrounds, normalizes photometric flux scaling, computes difference and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) maps, detects and cross-matches astronomical sources, converts pixel positions back into celestial coordinates, and renders an annotated false-color PNG accompanied by a quantitative analysis summary that flags candidate moving, variable, newly appearing, or disappearing objects.

By automating complex astronomical calibration and image differencing behind an accessible visual interface, Astro Sentinella eliminates the steep technical barrier typically required to analyze raw multi-epoch space telescope data. Users need no specialized hardware or local installations, to inspect how the infrared sky evolves over time. The intended impact of the project is to facilitate access to SPHEREx’s data, empowering students, educators, citizen scientists, and researchers to accelerate discovery and create knowledge.

We developed the frontend of Astro Sentinella using React, TypeScript, and Vite to deliver a fast, modular, and responsive visual exploration experience. The backend API and astrophysical analysis pipeline were built in Python with Flask, integrating core scientific libraries including Astropy for FITS handling and WCS coordinate transformations, Reproject for spatial alignment, Photutils for two-dimensional background estimation, source detection, and aperture photometry, SciPy and NumPy for statistical noise suppression and array operations, and Matplotlib for rendering annotated false-color difference maps. The platform queries public NASA SPHEREx datasets through IRSA and was built on standard consumer laptops so the entire workflow runs smoothly on everyday devices.

Our creative approach unifies archive search and visual comparison into a single workflow that bridges visual intuition with quantitative astrophysics. Throughout development, our team carefully watched out for precise astrometric alignment across images, SPHEREx’s LVF wavelength shifts that can introduce stellar residuals when mismatched bands are compared, varying background gradients, resilient data caching to guarantee low-latency performance during high archive demand, and clear communication of statistical significance and measurement uncertainty. Full source code, technical documentation, and instructions on how to run Astro Sentinella locally are available in our public GitHub repository.

You can check out the code, documentation and a guide on how to run our project locally in our github repo!

*AI was used during the development of this project with different purposes:
Addressing specific research and technical questions
Suggesting code, accelerating tedious coding tasks, and debugging
Translation suggestions and corrections
